purpose: Building-safety drills, functional exercises and tabletops structured the way FEMA structures exercises (HSEEP), with Incident Command roles and an ICS-214 activity log for team play.
learner_wording_rule: Learner-facing copy says 'prepares you for' and links the official issuer. It never says certified, certificate earned here, or FEMA-certified.

hseep.title: Homeland Security Exercise and Evaluation Program (HSEEP), January 2020 revision

doctrine.automation_boundary: The runtime may draft EEG ratings, a hotwash record and an AAR/IP. A human evaluator finalises them; improvement-item owners are always assigned by a person.

scenarios.title: Fire and Smoke Evacuation

evidence: route choice away from smoke without elevator use

core_capabilities: On-scene Security, Protection, and Law Enforcement

objectives.text: Raise the alarm and call emergency services before investigating.
Evacuate by a route away from the reported smoke, without the passenger elevator.
Account for every occupant and hand off missing-person locations to responders.

eeg.task: Alarm activated and emergency services called
Smoke-free route selected; elevator not used; doors closed behind
Headcount reconciled at the alternate assembly area
Responder keep-clear held and handoff given; all-clear only from the fire service

hotwash_prompts: What went well, and why? (strengths)
What should be done differently next time? (areas for improvement)
Was any step of the plan unclear, missing or unsafe?
Who should own each fix, and by when?

learner_copy.summary: Smoke is reported near the east exit. Raise the alarm, pick a safe way out, and make sure everyone is counted.

scenarios.safety_boundary: Simulation only. Occupants never fight a fire in this drill; extinguisher use is not taught here.

scenarios.title: Shelter in Place for Severe Weather

objectives.text: Confirm the warning from an official source and choose shelter over evacuation.
Move everyone, including visitors, to an interior area away from glass.
Hold until an official all-clear and keep a headcount.

eeg.task: Warning confirmed and shelter decision made
Clear announcement and move to interior shelter
Headcount and official all-clear

hotwash_prompts: What went well, and why? (strengths)
What should be done differently next time? (areas for improvement)
Was any step of the plan unclear, missing or unsafe?
Who should own each fix, and by when?

learner_copy.summary: A severe weather warning is issued for the area. Decide whether to stay or go, and get everyone somewhere safe inside.

scenarios.safety_boundary: Simulation only. The interior shelter area is a training choice in the virtual building, not a certified storm shelter.

scenarios.title: Active Threat Awareness (Tabletop)

content_policy.guidance_source: FEMA IS-907.A and DHS/CISA Active Shooter Preparedness: Run, Hide, Fight. Equity Uprise adds nothing beyond that guidance.

evidence: run-hide-fight decision order per official guidance

objectives.text: Describe the Run, Hide, Fight order from official guidance.
Describe when and how to call 911 and how to act when police arrive.
Describe how people are accounted for and reunified afterwards.

eeg.task: Run, Hide, Fight order stated in sequence
911 call when safe; hands visible when police arrive
Accountability and reunification described

hotwash_prompts: What went well, and why? (strengths)
What should be done differently next time? (areas for improvement)
Was any step of the plan unclear, missing or unsafe?
Who should own each fix, and by when?

learner_copy.summary: A discussion exercise about what to do if someone reports an active threat in the building. Nothing is shown; you talk through the official Run, Hide, Fight guidance.

scenarios.safety_boundary: Discussion only. Non-graphic. No weapons, attackers or injuries are depicted, and no tactics beyond the official FEMA/DHS guidance are taught.

scenarios.title: Hazardous Materials Release at the Service Entrance

evidence: hazard recognition from outside the area

objectives.text: Recognise an unknown release and isolate the area without entering or cleaning up.
Report and move people upwind to a safe assembly area.
Keep the responder area clear and hand off to hazmat responders.

eeg.task: Area isolated with no entry or clean-up attempt
Report made; upwind protective action chosen
Keep-clear held; all-clear only from responders

hotwash_prompts: What went well, and why? (strengths)
What should be done differently next time? (areas for improvement)
Was any step of the plan unclear, missing or unsafe?
Who should own each fix, and by when?

learner_copy.summary: A strong chemical smell is reported at the delivery entrance. Keep people away, report it, and move everyone upwind.

scenarios.safety_boundary: Simulation only. No entry, identification, containment or clean-up instruction; the spill kit is not for unknown releases.

scenarios.title: Full Building Evacuation, B1 to Roof, with Tunnel Headcount

objectives.text: Establish command and sweep every floor from B1 to the roof by the protected stairs.
Reconcile B1 and tunnel occupancy without touching live underground controls.
Produce a whole-building headcount and hand unaccounted persons to responders.

eeg.task: Command established; panel checked by the safety officer
Upper floors swept by Stair A/B; stairwells discharge at Level 1
B1 exits upward; tunnel roster reconciled; nothing live unlocked
Headcount reconciled and handed off; no re-entry

hotwash_prompts: What went well, and why? (strengths)
What should be done differently next time? (areas for improvement)
Was any step of the plan unclear, missing or unsafe?
Who should own each fix, and by when?
hseep.nfpa_note: NFPA 101 requires drills in business occupancies above certain occupant loads or when more than 100 people are above or below the level of exit discharge; B1 and F2-L7 are above or below it. Frequency is set by the adopted code and the local authority having jurisdiction.

learner_copy.summary: The general alarm sounds in every part of the building, from B1 to the roof. Run the whole evacuation as a team and prove everyone is out, including anyone in the tunnel.

scenarios.safety_boundary: Functional exercise in the SANDBOX building: people and resources move only in simulation. No live tunnel, door or alarm control.

scenarios.title: Disability-Inclusive Evacuation
scenarios.privacy_rule: The evacuation-assistance register is voluntary and confidential. The drill uses synthetic codes only; no names, conditions or medical details exist in the scenario, the runtime or the evidence.

objectives.text: Use the voluntary, confidential assistance register and assign helpers.
Move to the assisted evacuation point at the protected stair and keep communication open.
Hand locations of people awaiting assistance to responders and account for everyone.

eeg.task: Register used confidentially; two helpers assigned; person asked how to help
Assisted evacuation point reached without the elevator; mobility device kept with the person
Locations handed off; everyone including helpers accounted for

hotwash_prompts: What went well, and why? (strengths)
What should be done differently next time? (areas for improvement)
Was any step of the plan unclear, missing or unsafe?
Who should own each fix, and by when?

learner_copy.summary: The alarm sounds and someone on Floor 3 has asked, in advance and in confidence, for help evacuating. Plan and carry out an evacuation that leaves nobody behind.

scenarios.safety_boundary: Simulation only. The ADA does not itself require an evacuation plan, but a plan that exists must include people with disabilities. Elevator use in an emergency is decided by the fire service, never assumed.

scenarios.title: Building Emergency Plan versus Community EOP (Tabletop)

objectives.text: Check the building's emergency action plan against the OSHA 1910.38 minimum elements.
Identify where the building plan relies on the community emergency operations plan.
Record gaps as owned improvement items.

eeg.task: All six EAP elements checked
Community EOP dependencies named
Improvement items recorded and AAR/IP drafted

hotwash_prompts: What went well, and why? (strengths)
What should be done differently next time? (areas for improvement)
Was any step of the plan unclear, missing or unsafe?
Who should own each fix, and by when?

learner_copy.summary: A discussion exercise: read the building's emergency plan, compare it with what the town's emergency plan expects, and write down what needs fixing.

scenarios.safety_boundary: Discussion only. The virtual building's plan is a teaching artifact, not a compliance review.
